name: Zuo Jiaping
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Linkerbot (灵心巧手), Beijing; role not confirmed in public sources
profile: Hurun's 2026 unicorn-founder list names Zuo Jiaping as a founder of Linkerbot, a Beijing maker of dexterous robotic hands (Linker Hand). Public reporting names Zhou Yong (Alex Zhou) as founder/CEO and Zhang Yanbai as co-founder; no public source found linking the name Zuo Jiaping to the company.
interesting_fact: Linkerbot's Linker Hand line is reported to hold roughly 80% of the global market for high-degree-of-freedom dexterous robot hands (company/media claim).
notes: Could not verify this person's identity or role (searched English and Chinese name variants). Possibly a Hurun transliteration/listing issue. Company-level outreach would go via Linkerbot; founder Zhou Yong and co-founder Zhang Yanbai are the public faces.

name: Vivek Veda
profile: Chartered accountant and former equity/banking analyst who co-founded Bengaluru digital lender KreditBee (with Madhusudan Ekambaram and Karthikeyan Krishnaswamy) and serves as its CFO. KreditBee offers instant personal loans to millions of Indian consumers and was valued around $2B per Hurun.
interesting_fact: KreditBee has said it has disbursed over Rs 30,000 crore in loans to some 5 crore (50 million) users through a fully online process.
deep_cut_fact: He is also a co-founder of FACE (Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment), the industry body launched in October 2020 that later became the RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisation for India's fintech sector.
notes: Low public profile; speaks mostly to fintech/finance trade press (ET CFO, Elets, IBS Intelligence). Company contact page lists only customer support (help@kreditbee.in), not a press line.

name: Kirill Bigai
profile: Ukrainian co-founder and CEO of Preply, the online language-tutoring marketplace he started in Kyiv in 2012 with Dmytro Voloshyn and Serge Lukyanov. Preply connects learners with ~100,000 tutors; in January 2026 it raised a $150M Series D led by WestCap at a $1.2B valuation and is EBITDA-profitable. He is now pushing AI features (lesson summaries, homework, tutor matching).
interesting_fact: Preply grew out of his own struggle to find an English tutor online; it reached unicorn status in 2026 while keeping around 150 of its ~750 staff in wartime Kyiv.
deep_cut_fact: Before Preply he was an Intelligent Network Engineer at Ukrainian Vodafone; his first startup, FindGuru (a marketplace for local group classes), was sparked in 2011 when he struggled to find a Chinese teacher. He also taught himself SEO and consulted on it to fund the early days.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO (TechCrunch, Fortune, Forbes Ukraine interviews). Says soccer and strategy games shaped his thinking. Press route: press@preply.com.

name: Adam Israel
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Commercial Officer, Mesh (San Francisco crypto payments network)
profile: Veteran of three decades in traditional finance (JPMorgan Chase, HSBC broker-dealer and high-net-worth banking operations) who co-founded Mesh with CEO Bam Azizi in 2020. Mesh builds a blockchain-based payment network connecting exchanges, wallets and merchants; in January 2026 it raised a $75M Series C led by Dragonfly at a $1B valuation, taking total funding past $200M.
interesting_fact: Part of Mesh's funding rounds was settled in stablecoins (including PayPal's PYUSD) - the company's own proof that onchain settlement works for large transactions.
deep_cut_fact: He moved into crypto after roughly 30 years in Wall Street finance; his first crypto role was at Alto (alternative-asset IRAs), where its integration with Coinbase 'opened up my eyes' to the space. He holds an NYU MBA in finance.
notes: Title varies by source (COO in older interviews; CCO on current Mesh site). A reprint of the Series C release reportedly lists Mission North (mesh@missionnorth.com) as Mesh's PR agency, but I could not verify it on the original release, so it is not listed as a contact. CEO Bam Azizi is the main public face.
